blurb: Worth flagging for any Perimeter-area parent who's survived a summer of "I'm bored" — Altitude Trampoline Park in Marietta is a short drive up Lower Roswell Road and the kind of place that genuinely wears kids out. We're talking wall-to-wall trampolines, basketball dunking lanes, foam pits, and enough stations that kids rotate through without you having to manage any of it. Multiple reviewers specifically call out the birthday party experience: easy booking, responsive staff, and an event that actually ran smoothly from arrival to cake. That combination is rarer than it sounds. Camp groups have also used it as a field trip stop, and the consensus is that kids stay engaged the entire time — no one's standing around looking at their phone. At 4.7 stars across 840 reviews, the rating reflects a place that has figured out operations. It sits outside the core Dunwoody/Sandy Springs/Brookhaven footprint, but for families in the Perimeter area it's close enough to make it onto a weekend shortlist.

blurb: If you've been half-heartedly meaning to get back into a gym routine, this one on Hammond Drive in Dunwoody is worth a real look. Onelife Fitness at Perimeter Sports Club is a full-service facility that members consistently describe as clean, well-run, and reasonably priced — which, in the Atlanta fitness market, is not something you can take for granted. What actually sets it apart is the indoor movie theater with treadmills as the seats. You show up to get your cardio in and end up 40 minutes into a film before you notice you've been running. The rest of the club holds up too: solid equipment, locker rooms that don't make you wince, and a sauna (one longtime member's note: get the burner fixed, guys — four years is long enough). At 4.4 stars across 773 reviews, this isn't a gym people are staying out of loyalty to a sunk cost. They're staying because it works. Right in the heart of Perimeter, so no excuse about the commute.
